text:
Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.66% today after falling sharply over the previous two trading days. The modest gain came as oil prices pulled back from session highs on news of potential talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a major chokepoint for global crude shipments; the geopolitical uncertainty that had lifted prices earlier in the week eased slightly. Refineries are running near capacity at 94%, but the conflicting signals—diesel prices at $6.51 per gallon sparking calls for an export ban, yet industry warnings that such a ban would ultimately raise fuel costs—leave the near-term direction of refining margins unclear.

The stock's sharp 8% decline from September 17 to September 22 reflected real anxiety about policy intervention in diesel markets and ongoing Iran-related geopolitical risk. Today's stabilization suggests some traders are taking a breather as the market digests competing narratives: tighter crude supplies from Middle East tensions versus the possibility of negotiated de-escalation and potential policy headwinds for refiners.
